summary: Conservation dominates: Guyana reports forest at approximately 85% of the national territory and 18 million hectares at end-2022, and targets annual emissions reductions of 21,653,431 tCO2e from sustainable forest management and conservation (0.1% of forest carbon stock). It commits 50% of GFC staff to field monitoring, rising to 60% by 2030 and 65% by 2035; carbon-credit revenue is intended to benefit 80% of Indigenous villages and communities by 2030 and 100% by 2035. The agriculture pledge uses carbon-market revenues from 2016-2025 to sustainably irrigate 100,000 acres and strengthen drainage and irrigation resilience; this is about 405 km2, or 14.5% of mapped agricultural area (2,797 km2). The 18-million-hectare estimate corresponds to about 91.6% of mapped forest (196,477 km2, 92.8% of country).
